### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **3** package(s): `@objectstack/mcp`, `@objectstack/platform-objects`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **10** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **3** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/authorable-surface/ai.json`, `packages/spec/liveness/skill.json`, `packages/spec/liveness/state-counts/skill.md`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**3** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx`  _(via mcpPrompt (literal, a string literal in sections))_
- `content/docs/ai/connect-mcp.mdx`  _(via mcpPrompt (literal, a string literal in sections))_
- `content/docs/ai/skills.mdx`  _(via SkillSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_

⛔ **1** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-0.mdx`  _(via SkillSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **3** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/authorable-surface/ai.json`, `packages/spec/liveness/skill.json`, `packages/spec/liveness/state-counts/skill.md`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **2** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **178** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json b51cb18a752779c412f12b87603aa75f4023659e` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `a3c56f26e849389ab8d7974f6b0b3142db83b37d` — the merge of head `50ccfc48fb6776a7e31d050e6592d75ca6f41704` into base `b51cb18a752779c412f12b87603aa75f4023659e`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin a3c56f26e849389ab8d7974f6b0b3142db83b37d && git checkout a3c56f26e849389ab8d7974f6b0b3142db83b37d
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin b51cb18a752779c412f12b87603aa75f4023659e 50ccfc48fb6776a7e31d050e6592d75ca6f41704 && git checkout -B drift-repro b51cb18a752779c412f12b87603aa75f4023659e && git merge --no-ff 50ccfc48fb6776a7e31d050e6592d75ca6f41704

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json b51cb18a752779c412f12b87603aa75f4023659e
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs b51cb18a752779c412f12b87603aa75f4023659e` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `50ccfc48fb6776a7e31d050e6592d75ca6f41704`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/ai/skill.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/ai/skill.form.ts + packages/mcp/src/skill-prompts.ts, packages/spec/liveness/skill.json, packages/spec/authorable-surface/ai.json, content/docs/ai/agents.mdx, content/docs/ai/connect-mcp.mdx, content/docs/references/ai/skill.mdx

Read from card #34167 (body and its three comments), the PR body and file list, the net diff `origin/main...50ccfc48` (merge base `571cf908`, `main` at `98a4449f`), and the head's check-runs. Read but not reviewed: `packages/mcp/src/mcp-server-runtime.ts`, `packages/runtime/src/domains/mcp.ts`, `ui/packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/SchemaForm.tsx`.

Check-runs at this head, at the last read: 19 concluded `success`, 10 `skipped`, none failed, 35 still `in_progress`. Concluded green and relevant here: Spec property liveness, Check Changeset, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Lint · PM dispatch-gates, Lint · ESLint, Lint · repo & tooling gates, Type Check · source gates, Build Docs, Check Documentation Links, PR-body guards. Still running: Test Core 1/8 to 8/8, Test UI 1/16 to 16/16, Build Core, Build & E2E UI, Live E2E UI, Type Check UI, Type Check (workspace, debt ledger, consumer gates) and four Lint jobs (CI/release/engine gates, docs and code guards, query-options erasure, slot lookup and corpus). This verdict covers what had concluded; the test shards and the workspace type check had not, and the seat reads them before landing.

### ① Derived judgments

- **Accept-set, `SkillSchema`: one new optional key, `mcpPrompt: boolean`. Right.** `z.boolean().optional()` with no default inside the existing `strictObject`. A document that parsed on `main` parses the same; a document carrying a boolean `mcpPrompt`, refused on `main` as an unknown key, is now accepted. Nothing is refused that was accepted. A widening.
- **Parsed shape for a row without the key: unchanged. Right.** No default and no transform, so the parse output gains no key. The other keys of the schema are edited in JSDoc and `describe` text only.
- **Published text: the `describe` strings of `instructions` and `tools` change. Right.** They move the generated reference page and the JSON Schema descriptions, not the accept-set.
- **MCP prompt surface: narrower only for rows that set `mcpPrompt: false`. Right.** The one new line in `projectSkillPrompt` is a strict `=== false`. Absent, `true`, or a non-boolean on an unvalidated raw row all project as on `main`. No skill on `main` can carry the key, since the strict schema refuses it, so no existing skill projects differently and there is no narrowing arm to declare.
- **HTTP (`registerSkillPrompts`): right.** Both handlers read `listSkillPromptsServedBy`, which calls `projectSkillPrompt` per row. A declared row is absent from `prompts/list`, and `prompts/get` reaches the same `not-found` branch and the same `-32602` as an unknown name. `readMergedSkillRows` in `packages/runtime/src/domains/mcp.ts` hands the rows over whole, so the key reaches the reader on the real endpoint.
- **stdio (`bridgePrompts`), key present at boot: right.** The boot snapshot, each registered prompt's re-read and the bare-name route all go through `listSkillPrompts`. A row declared at boot is never registered and never got.
- **stdio, key set while the server runs: wrong against the published sentence.** See ④, finding 1.
- **No other lister or resolver.** `agent_prompt` (`buildAgentPromptResult`) serves the agent's own instructions and reads no skill. No MCP resource or tool in `packages/mcp/src` reads `skill` rows. `skill-md.ts` is the other "skill" and is untouched.
- **In-product agents, `surface`, `tools`: right as far as this repository can show.** No file in the diff touches a reader of `surface`, `tools`, `triggerConditions` or `active`, and the only in-repo readers of the wiring half are the two lint validators, unchanged. The in-product runtime lives in cloud and was not read; the claim that it ignores the key rests on the key being new and is cloud#4337's to confirm.
- **Ledgers: right.** `authorable-surface/ai.json` gains `ai/Skill:mcpPrompt`; `liveness/skill.json` gains a `live` row whose anchor `packages/mcp/src/skill-prompts.ts#projectSkillPrompt` is local and resolves to the line that reads the key; the state count moves 16 to 17.

### ② Semver level

Clause-②: yes (widening). Correct, and the PR body and changeset agree.
Metadata-protocol: added. Correct: a new key a metadata author can write.

AGENTS.md, Post-Task Checklist item 3: a kind takes at least `minor` on a package the diff moves. The changeset is `minor` on `@objectstack/spec` (the key), `@objectstack/mcp` (the reader) and `@objectstack/platform-objects` (the regenerated form catalogs). `@objectstack/lint` and `@objectstack/metadata-protocol` change in test files only and publish nothing. The level matches what the diff publishes. Not breaking, so no migration and no ADR-0087 disposition is owed. `Check Changeset` concluded `success`.

One sentence of the changeset body is wrong against the tree: it says the form offers the toggle "in its Basics section". `skill.form.ts` puts it in the "AI Instructions" section. Graded in ④, finding 3.

### ③ Boundary flags

- `open_questions`: empty. Nothing to answer.
- `out_of_scope_findings`, "Skills-docs follow-up owed: `skills/objectstack-ai/SKILL.md` should name `mcpPrompt`; carrier: server seat 7 files it": **escalated to the seat.** The PR body carries the matching `Skills-docs: follow-up owed` line, and `skills/` is outside this PR's surface, so leaving it out is right. No follow-up card is cited anywhere in the inputs; the seat files it before landing.
- Claim flag, "any existing skill that would project differently is declared as a narrowing arm": **answered, none exists** (① above).
- Claim flag, "Metadata-protocol: derived in the shape note" and "every file is named in a shape note before code": **escalated to the seat.** The card thread holds a triage comment, the claim and the dev report, and no shape note. The value `added` is right on the merits; the note itself is the seat's to locate or waive.
- Claim file surface: the diff also touches `packages/spec/src/ai/skill.form.ts`, the `platform-objects` catalogs and pin test, and pin tests in `packages/lint` and `packages/metadata-protocol`. The form and catalogs follow from the gates a new authorable key trips, and the rest are test pins. **Answered: within the claim's "generated artefacts its gates demand"**; the remainder is the lane seat's ACCEPT.
- `security_findings`: none reported, and none found in scope.

### ④ Design judgment

**`packages/spec/src/ai/skill.zod.ts` (hit).** Holds against the card. Done-when 1 is met for a declared skill on both doors, with the caveat in finding 1. Done-when 2 holds: no default, the #32767 binding code is untouched, and a skill without the key takes the same path as on `main`. Done-when 3 holds as far as this repository reaches. Done-when 4 holds: the `mcpPrompt`, `instructions` and `tools` text all say how a skill opts out. The choice of a separate key over a new `surface` member is sound, because `surface` is read by the in-product runtime and a new member would change that read.

**`packages/mcp/src/skill-prompts.ts` (implementing).** The code agrees with its own header and with the schema JSDoc. One strict check, placed where both doors read. Attempts to break it that failed: a row with `mcpPrompt: true`; a declared row beside an undeclared row of the same name in another package (the declared one is dropped before faces are grouped, so the other is served alone); a declared row sharing a face with another (same); the binding filter running first (it cannot bring a row back).

**Finding 1, should-fix. The "never, on every connection, stdio included" sentence is false for a skill switched off while the stdio server is running.** `bridgePrompts` registers the prompt list once at boot. Its get callback re-reads, and when the re-read no longer finds the face it falls back to the boot snapshot (`mcp-server-runtime.ts:2470` to `2471`, "Gone since the snapshot: the snapshot's one skill, as before"). So a skill that was undeclared at boot and is then saved with `mcpPrompt: false` (the runtime `PUT /api/v1/meta/skill/NAME` that `mergedRead` exists to carry, and the path the new form toggle writes) stays in `prompts/list` and is still answered by `prompts/get`, with its boot-time instructions, until the process restarts. HTTP drops it at once. The same holds on `main` for `active: false`, and the fallback line is outside this diff. What is in the diff is the unqualified sentence, in five places: the `mcpPrompt` JSDoc and `describe` in `skill.zod.ts`, the header of `skill-prompts.ts`, the `evidence` of the liveness row, `agents.mdx` ("on every MCP connection, stdio included") and `connect-mcp.mdx` ("on every connection (HTTP and stdio)"). Either qualify those sentences (on the long-lived stdio server the prompt list is taken at boot, so a change made while it runs takes effect on restart), or make the stdio get stop serving the snapshot for a row the re-read shows as opted out, with a pin. Graded should-fix and not must-fix because the card's case, a skill declared in its package source, is read at boot and is withheld on both doors; the gap is a bounded window on one transport that `main` already has for `active`.

**`packages/spec/src/ai/skill.form.ts` (hit).**

**Finding 2, should-fix. The toggle shows "off" for every skill that is in fact offered.** The field is a bare boolean, and Studio's `SchemaForm` renders it as a switch with `checked={!!value}` (`SchemaForm.tsx:2492`). The key has no default, so on every skill without it (every skill that exists today) the control labelled "Offer as MCP prompt" reads off while the code offers the skill. An author who opens the form to opt a playbook out sees it already off and has nothing to do; writing `false` takes turning the switch on and then off again. The help text ends "Unset = offered", which is correct, but a two-state switch cannot show unset, so the control and its help text disagree. This is the one place where the form does not say what the code does. The fix is a control whose unset state does not read as off, for example a select with an explicit "Offered (default)" entry as `surface` uses, or whatever the form kit offers for an optional boolean whose absence means yes. A schema default is not the fix: it would change the parsed shape the PR promises to leave alone.

**Finding 3, nit.** The changeset body and the PR body say the toggle is in the form's "Basics" section; it is in "AI Instructions". One word in the changeset, which ships as CHANGELOG text. No effect on the contract.

**Finding 4, nit.** The new field sets `colSpan: 1` in a section that declares no `columns`; the two fields beside it set none. Harmless.

**`packages/spec/liveness/skill.json` (implementing).** Agrees with the code apart from finding 1. Its note says the cloud agent runtime does not read the key; that is a cross-repo statement on an `in-repo` row. It sits in the `note`, not the `evidence`, so the gate reads nothing false, and no cloud row is re-stamped.

**`packages/spec/authorable-surface/ai.json` (implementing).** Agrees: one row, in sorted position.

**`content/docs/ai/agents.mdx`, `content/docs/ai/connect-mcp.mdx` (implementing).** Agree with the code sentence by sentence apart from finding 1. The example in `connect-mcp.mdx` uses `defineSkill` with keys the schema accepts.

**`content/docs/references/ai/skill.mdx` (implementing).** Generated; its three changed rows match the `describe` strings exactly.

Findings 1 and 2 earn a delta review. Neither is a must-fix.
